'''Vinod Johri''' (10 June 1935 – 10 May 2014) was an Indian [[astrophysicist]]. He was an eminent [[cosmologist]], a retired professor of [[astrophysics]] at [[Indian Institute of Technology]], [[Madras]] and an emeritus professor at [[Lucknow University]] since 1995. Johri had over 75 research publications and articles published in pioneering journals. His major contributions in cosmological research included 'power law inflation, genesis of [[Quintessence (physics)|quintessence]] fields of [[dark energy]] and phantom cosmologies'. He was the co-author of the first model of power law inflation in [[Brans–Dicke theory]] along with C. Mathiazhagan. He was honored by [[Uttar Pradesh Government]] by Research Award of the Council of Science & Technology (CSIR).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cstup.gov.in/ |title=Cst U.P |publisher=Cst U.P. |access-date=21 October 2011 |archive-date=10 February 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210101544/http://cstup.gov.in/ }}</ref>

Johri spent over 45 years researching in cosmology, acting as a research guide and principal investigator of various research projects of Council of Scientific and Industrial Research,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://rdpp.csir.res.in/csir_acsir/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=1 January 2011 |archive-date=14 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100914224802/http://rdpp.csir.res.in/csir_acsir/ }}</ref> Department of Science & Technology<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.serc-dst.org/ |title=Welcome to Science And Engineering Research Council |publisher=Serc-dst.org |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> and University Grants Commission of India.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ugc.ac.in/ |title=:::Welcome to UGC ::: |publisher=Ugc.ac.in |date=18 June 2004 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> Johri was a Commonwealth Fellow, a senior visitor at Cambridge University (UK) and a Fellow of Royal Astronomical Society<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ras.org.uk/ |title=The Royal Astronomical Society |publisher=Ras.org.uk |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> of London. He worked as consultant for [[UNESCO]] at United Nations Development Program<ref>{{cite web|author=Pooneh Tehrani |url=http://www.unic-ir.org/ |title=::::: United Nations Information Centre, Tehran ::::: |publisher=Unic-ir.org |date=19 April 2010 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> in [[Iran]] and as a DAAD Fellow<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.daad.org/ |title=Home |publisher=Daad.org |date=13 November 2010 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> at [[University of Mainz]] (Germany), as a visiting scientist at Hansen Lab<ref>{{cite web|author=Ronald K. Hanson |url=http://hanson.stanford.edu/ |title=The Hanson Group: Home |publisher=Hanson.stanford.edu |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> (Gravity Probe B Group) [[Stanford University]] (USA) and as an International Scholar at Fine Theoretical Physics Institute<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ftpi.umn.edu/research/|title=Research &#124; William I. Fine Theoretical Physics Institute &#124; College of Science and Engineering|access-date=1 January 2011|archive-date=20 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720092516/http://www.ftpi.umn.edu/research/|url-status=dead}}</ref> at [[University of Minnesota]] at Minneapolis (USA). He died in Dallas, USA at the age of 78 due to complications arising from Kidney failure.

==Career==
Johri was born in [[Etah]] ([[Uttar Pradesh]]), India, on 10 June 1935. His father, Bhairon Prasad Johri, graduated from Veterinary College, [[Patna]], and worked as livestock officer, Allahabad, India. Johri's mother, Sarojini Johri, was a homemaker.

Johri completed his high school at Narain College,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://naraincollege.com/ |title=Education - Home |access-date=5 February 2010 |archive-date=10 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100910100717/http://naraincollege.com/ }}</ref> [[Shikohabad]], India, with 12th rank in the state merit list. He was awarded First Prize in Chiranjeevi Dhiri Singh Provincial English Debate. He completed his bachelor's degree in 1953 and master's in [[applied mathematics]] in 1956 from [[Allahabad University]] scoring high ranks in the merit list. In 1957 he was appointed as assistant professor in the Department of Mathematics Allahabad University,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.alldunivpio.org/ |title=Home |website=alldunivpio.org}}</ref> [[Allahabad]]. In 1960, Johri was appointed assistant professor in mathematics at Gorakhpur University,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ddugu.edu.in/ |title=Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University, Gorakhpur..A NAAC Accredited B++ University |publisher=Ddugu.edu.in |date=16 October 2011 |access-date=21 October 2011 |archive-date=14 October 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111014002304/http://www.ddugu.edu.in/ }}</ref> [[Gorakhpur]] India, where he was conferred PhD degree in 1966 on his thesis "Gravitational Waves in Bondi Space-Time".

In 1967 Johri was awarded Commonwealth Fellowship for Post-Doctorate work at Department of Mathematics and Theoretical Physics,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/ |title=DAMTP |publisher=Damtp.cam.ac.uk |date=12 April 2011 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> Cambridge University (UK), where he worked in close collaboration on cosmological problems with Dr.[[Dennis Sciama]] and research scholars Friedrich Hehl (Cologne), Fernando de Felice<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rssd.esa.int/index.php?project=GAIA&page=Gaia_people&person=72&ordering=alphabetical |title=Gaia: People working on Gaia |publisher=Rssd.esa.int |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> (Padova, Italy), [[George Francis Rayner Ellis|George Ellis]] (Cape Town) and [[Stephen Hawking]] (UK) for his postdoctoral program. In 1968 Johri was appointed reader in mathematics at [[Gorakhpur University]]. Between 1970 and 1972, Johri worked as [[UNESCO]] consultant to [[Government of Iran]] under [[United Nations Development Program]] at Tehran. Johri was elected a Fellow of [[Royal Astronomical Society]] of London in 1978.

Johri accepted the position of professor of cosmology at the Mathematics Department of Indian Institute of Technology,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iitm.ac.in/ |title=IIT Madras Home |publisher=Iitm.ac.in |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> Madras ([[Chennai]]) in 1980. In addition to teaching and advising PhD students, he introduced new courses on [[general relativity]] and [[cosmology]]. In 1984, he discovered the first model of 'power law inflation' under [[Brans–Dicke theory]] (later on called as 'extended inflation') along with his student C.Mathizhagan. Johri worked on various visiting assignments at National University<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kuniv.edu.kw/ |title=Kuwait University |publisher=Kuniv.edu.kw |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> (Kuwait), [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]], [[Trieste]] (Italy), Copernicus Astronomical Institute, [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (Warsaw), [[National University of Singapore]], South West Technical [[University of Sydney]]; [[Australian National University]], [[Canberra]], Hansen Lab (Gravity Probe B Group),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://einstein.stanford.edu/Media/ |title=Gravity Probe B&nbsp;– Media Galleries |publisher=Einstein.stanford.edu |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> [[Stanford University]], [[Cologne University]], [[International Institute of Physics]] and Chemistry [[Université libre de Bruxelles|Brussels University]] (hosted by Nobel Laureate Prof. [[Ilya Prigogine]]).

In 1995 Johri retired from Indian Institute of Technology<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iitm.ac.in/ |title=IIT Madras Home |publisher=Iitm.ac.in |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> and joined as CSIR<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cstup.gov.in/ |title=Cst U.P |publisher=Cst U.P. |access-date=21 October 2011 |archive-date=10 February 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210101544/http://cstup.gov.in/ }}</ref> Professor Emeritus in the Department of Mathematics & Astronomy at Lucknow University,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lkouniv.ac.in/ |title=Lucknow University !!! |publisher=Lkouniv.ac.in |date=9 February 2009 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> [[Lucknow]] (India). In 2001, Johri got interested in [[dark energy]] during his visiting assignment at Fine Theoretical Physics Institute,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.physics.umn.edu/ |title=Home Page&nbsp;– Physics at Minnesota |publisher=Physics.umn.edu |date=27 May 2011 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> [[University of Minnesota]] (USA), he gave the theory of 'integrated tracking' of Quintessence Fields. His research work on 'Genesis of Quintessence'<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://prd.aps.org/abstract/PRD/v63/i10/e103504 |title=Phys. Rev. D 63, 103504 (2001): Genesis of cosmological tracker fields |journal=Physical Review D |date=12 April 2001 |volume=63 |issue=10 |article-number=103504 |publisher=Prd.aps.org |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.63.103504 |access-date=21 October 2011|last1=Johri |first1=Vinod B. |s2cid=14180304 |arxiv=astro-ph/0005608 }}</ref> and 'Phantom Cosmologies'<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://prd.aps.org/abstract/PRD/v70/i4/e041303 |title=Phys. Rev. D 70, 041303 (2004): Phantom cosmologies |journal=Physical Review D |date=24 August 2004 |volume=70 |issue=4 |article-number=041303 |publisher=Prd.aps.org |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.70.041303 |access-date=21 October 2011|last1=Johri |first1=Vinod B. |s2cid=119064944 |url-access=subscription |arxiv=astro-ph/0311293 }}</ref> was published in reputed journals [[Physical Review]] D & [[Classical and Quantum Gravity]].

==Honors==
Johri was a [[Commonwealth Fellow]] and a senior visitor to Cambridge University (UK). He was also a resident of Clare College, Cambridge. He was elected a Fellow of [[Royal Astronomical Society]] of London in 1978. Johri was awarded the Royal Society Visiting Fellowship in 1989 for visiting Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics (DAMTP) Cambridge,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/ |title=DAMTP |publisher=Damtp.cam.ac.uk |date=12 April 2011 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> [[Southampton University]] (UK), [[Cardiff University]] and [[Queen Mary College]], London under the Distinguished Scientists Exchange Program of British Council.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.britishcouncil.org/new/ |title=British Council |publisher=British Council |date=25 October 2010 |access-date=21 October 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111020230845/http://www.britishcouncil.org/new/ |archive-date=20 October 2011 }}</ref> In 1993, Johri was awarded [[German Academic Exchange Service|DAAD]] Fellowship for his visiting assignment at Theoretical Physics Institute, [[Johannes Gutenberg University]], [[Mainz]](Germany).

Johri was honored with a 'Silver Plaque' by Council of Science & Technology,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cstup.gov.in/ |title=Cst U.P |publisher=Cst U.P. |access-date=21 October 2011 |archive-date=10 February 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210101544/http://cstup.gov.in/ }}</ref> India for his distinguished work on Dark Energy in the year 2006. He was Life Member of Ganita Parishad<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lkouniv.ac.in/dept_math.htm |title=Lucknow University !!! |publisher=Lkouniv.ac.in |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> and a founding member of the Indian Association of General Relativity and Gravitation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.imsc.res.in/~iagrg/ |title=<!-- Main page of the site, entry-point --> IAGRG Home Page |publisher=Imsc.res.in |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref>

==Writings and hobbies==
Besides scientific research papers and popular science articles, Johri wrote several books on Mathematical Physics and Astrophysics. His research monograph ''Early Universe'' was published by Hadronic Press (USA) in 1996.
Vinod Johri loved to compose verses in Hindi, Urdu and English during his leisure time.

==Personal life==
Johri was married to Aruna (maiden name Kodesia) for 54 years. The couple had 2 sons Manoj (Software Architect, [[Hewlett-Packard|HP]]), Vivek (IT Manager, [[UnitedHealth Group]]) and 2 daughters Manisha (Teacher at Shishya,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sishya.com/ |title=Home |website=sishya.com}}</ref> Chennai) and Anvita (Software Development, [[UnitedHealth Group]]). Johri died on 10 May 2014, at the age of 78.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-20 |title=Vinod Johri: The Indian Cosmologist Who Explored the Universe - Kidz Herald |url=https://www.kidzherald.com/vinod-johri-the-indian-cosmologist-who-explored-the-universe/ |access-date=2024-12-12 |language=en-US}}</ref>
